title: This country is completely inside another country 🗺️ #shorts
description:
Lesotho is completely surrounded by South Africa. Only three countries on Earth sit entirely inside one other country, and Lesotho's lowest point is higher than the tallest mountain in Britain.

Sources
- Geography of Lesotho (area 30,355 km², enclaved, lowest point 1,400 m): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geography_of_Lesotho
- Belgium (area 30,689 km²): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium
- Ben Nevis (1,345 m): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Nevis
- Map outlines: Natural Earth (public domain), equal-area projection: https://www.naturalearthdata.com/

title: How many Earths fit inside the Sun? ☀️ #shorts
description:
109 Earths across its face, about 1.3 million to fill it, and 99.8% of all the mass in our solar system.

Sources
- NASA — Sun facts (≈1.3 million Earths, 99.8% of the mass): https://science.nasa.gov/sun/facts/
- NASA NSSDC — Sun fact sheet (radius 109 × Earth): https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/sunfact.html

title: 🐋 Every Giant Animal, True Size — Smallest to Largest Ever
description:
Was anything ever bigger than the blue whale? We line up every giant on the same ground, at true size, with one person as the ruler: from a bat the size of a bumblebee to crocodiles, giraffes, elephants, the biggest land mammal ever, a 10-metre flying reptile, Titanoboa, megalodon, Argentinosaurus and the new challengers from 2023 and 2024.

Every figure is sourced below. Estimates for extinct animals are marked as estimates on screen.

Chapters
0:00 A 30-metre animal
0:11 The only fair test
0:26 The smallest mammal
0:51 Saltwater crocodile
1:06 The tallest animal
1:21 The heaviest on land
1:41 Bigger than an elephant
2:02 The biggest flyer ever
2:22 The longest snakes
2:47 Why the sea grows giants
3:06 Sharks and squid
3:37 A 37-metre jellyfish?
3:53 Megalodon
4:20 The blue whale

5:22 New challengers
5:56 The verdict

title: Is the Moon bigger than your country? 🌕 #shorts
description:
The Moon is 3,475 km across: not wide enough to cover Australia or the United States. But its whole surface is almost exactly Africa plus Australia.

Sources
- NASA NSSDC — Moon fact sheet (diameter 3,474.8 km): https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/moonfact.html
- Geoscience Australia — continental extremities (≈4,000 km wide): https://www.ga.gov.au/scientific-topics/national-location-information/dimensions/continental-extremities
- Contiguous United States (≈4,500 km coast to coast): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contiguous_United_States
- Britannica — Moon (surface 37.9 million km²): https://www.britannica.com/place/Moon
- Britannica — Africa (30.37 million km²): https://www.britannica.com/place/Africa
- Map outlines: Natural Earth (public domain), equal-area projection: https://www.naturalearthdata.com/
